He further submits that the plaintiff claimed that the alleged deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz was obtained by fraud and, as such, the burden of proof was on him he who alleges fraud as to the execution of a document. In a case of Hussain Ahmed vs Sharifullah reported in 3 MLR (AD) 212, our apex court held that,— 

 "The burden of proof lies on him he who alleges fraud as to the execution of a document. When a power of attorney is not categorically denied and challenged as one being product of fraud and no evidence is led to prove the fact of fraud such document cannot be held to be fraudulent." 

 24. It further appears from the plaint that the plaintiff-petitioner stated in his plaint, nobody was present at Sub-registry office on behalf of the defendant, so the claim of influencing plaintiff-petitioner by defendant side is not proved at all. Now burden of proof was upon the plaintiff petitioner to prove his own case but he did not take any step to prove his case by adducing any corroborative witness except himself as PW 1. In this respect our apex court in a case reported in 4 XP (AD) 43 held that— 

 "It was found that only PW 1 was examined by the plaintiff on commission. But the plaintiff side did not examine any other witness to prove their positive case".  25. While adjudicating the appeal, the appellate court below observed that the plaintiff-appellant did not take any step to prove the fraud as alleged against the defendant No. 1 and in this case Rashedul Bari son of the appellant was the most competent witness who could prove the frauds but he was not examined by the appellant in trial or appeal stage although the burden of proof is lies upon the plaintiff-appellant and in this circumstances the appellate court below came to a conclusion that the appellant failed to prove his case by adducing evidence on record and finally disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court.
